samples.summary: PPTX color modifier attributes (`alpha`, `tint`, `shade`, `lumMod`, `lumOff`) are still interpolated raw after this change removed the file's only XML escaping
samples.evidence:
This diff deletes `import { escapeXmlAttr } from './xml.js'` from `color.ts` and replaces the escaped hex with `toRgbHexColor(c.value) ?? '000000'`, on the stated theory that normalization subsumes escaping. But lines 25-29 of the same function still do `mods.push(`<a:lumMod val="${c.lumMod}"/>`)` … `<a:alpha val="${c.alpha}"/>` with no coercion, and after this change nothing in the file escapes anything.

Vector: those fields are typed `number` but are *persisted JSON*. `packages/backend/src/yorkie/slides-tree.ts:101-104` assigns `root.slides = document.slides` verbatim, and `assertValidElement` (packages/backend/src/api/v1/docs-content.controller.ts:393-413) validates only `id`, `type` and `frame` — element `fill`/`stroke`/`effects` colors are never inspected. An authenticated workspace member (or an API key) PUTs an element whose fill is `{ kind: 'srgb', value: '#ffffff', alpha: '0"/><a:hlinkClick r:id="rId2' }`. When any user later exports the deck, `fillXml → solidFillXml → colorChildXml` emits `<a:alpha val="0"/><a:hlinkClick r:id="rId2"/>` — attacker-chosen OOXML elements inside the generated slide part.

The same sink is reachable from the function this diff actually rewrote: `packages/slides/src/export/pptx/text.ts:213-216` copies `out.tint = c.tint; out.shade = c.shade` straight off an untrusted docs `StoredColor` role object, so `{ kind:'role', role:'accent1', tint:'1"/><a:alpha val="0' }` on an inline style reaches `<a:tint val=…>` unescaped even though the srgb arm right above it is now normalized.

samples.summary: `ROLE_TO_SCHEME[c.role]` is a prototype-open object lookup — the exact pattern this change replaces with `Map` in the two alignment tables
samples.evidence: The diff introduces `DOCX_ALIGNMENTS`/`ALGN` as `Map`s specifically because "an object lookup consults the prototype chain … would survive the `?? 'left'` fallback and be stringified into the attribute". `colorChildXml` line 32 still does `const val = ROLE_TO_SCHEME[c.role]` on a plain object literal, with `c.role` typed `ColorRole` but sourced from persisted JSON (`root.slides` is stored verbatim; no element-style validation on the PUT path). `role: 'constructor'` yields `val="function Object() { [native code] }"`, `role: '__proto__'` yields `val="[object Object]"`. Neither inherited value contains a quote, so I could not turn this into attribute injection — impact is a schema-invalid deck rather than a break-out, hence minor — but it is the same open-lookup defect the change claims to have closed, and the guarantee is one added `Object.prototype` member (or a `role` string colliding with a future own key) away from mattering.

samples.summary: Design docs assert the OOXML color attributes are "injection-proof by construction", a guarantee that holds only for the `val` hex and not for the sibling attributes emitted by the same function
samples.evidence: `slides-pptx-export.md` ("The normalizer returns only `[0-9A-F]{6}`, which makes the attribute injection-proof by construction") and `docs-docx-import-export.md` ("Because the converter returns only `[0-9A-F]{6}`, these attributes are injection-proof by construction rather than by escaping") document a whole-sink guarantee. `colorChildXml` emits `<a:lumMod>/<a:lumOff>/<a:tint>/<a:shade>/<a:alpha>` from the same untrusted `ThemeColor` object with no converter and, after this diff, no escaping either. A future maintainer reading these docs will reasonably believe the color sink is covered and skip escaping when adding the next modifier attribute — the documented invariant is broader than the code enforces.

samples.summary: Docs body validation never visits header/footer blocks, which the writer dereferences unconditionally — an authenticated caller gets an unhandled TypeError (HTTP 500) instead of a 400
samples.evidence: `assertValidDocsBody` iterates only `body.blocks`. `writeDocsRoot → buildTreeChildren` (packages/backend/src/yorkie/docs-tree.ts:311-331) does `document.header.blocks.map(buildBlockNode)` with no guard, and `buildBlockNode` does `block.inlines.map(...)`. A PUT of `{"blocks":[],"header":{"marginFromEdge":0}}` — or `{"blocks":[],"header":{"marginFromEdge":0,"blocks":[{"id":"a","type":"paragraph","style":{}}]}}` — throws inside the `doc.update` callback and surfaces as a 500, contradicting the controller's own comment that validation exists so "a malformed payload would otherwise reach the writer and surface as HTTP 500 deep inside Yorkie". This diff extends that same comment block ("Shape only. Style *values* are not constrained here…") and leans on the writer being total for partial input, so the gap is squarely in the invariant the change is asserting. Impact is limited to a noisy 500 for an already-authenticated caller — `buildTreeChildren` runs before any tree mutation, so I could not show CRDT corruption.
searchedFor: grepped for 'header' and 'footer' handling in the controller's validators
checked whether writeDocsRoot mutates the tree before buildTreeChildren throws

verdict.reason: The described sink exists verbatim: color.ts:25-29 interpolates lumMod/lumOff/tint/shade/alpha into XML attribute values with no escaping and no numeric coercion, and the file no longer imports any escaping helper (escapeXmlAttr/attr live unused-by-color.ts at xml.ts:5-18); only c.value is normalized (color.ts:42). The values are attacker-controllable persisted JSON, not guaranteed numbers: text.ts:213-216 copies c.tint/c.shade off an untrusted StoredColor with no typeof check; model/migrate.ts:170-174 (wrapColor) returns any object with a `kind` field unchanged; backend assertValidElement validates only id/type/frame (docs-content.controller.ts:393-413) and writeSlidesRoot persists slides verbatim (slides-tree.ts:104). The sink is widely reachable (shape.ts:60,96,144; slide.ts:89; master.ts:31; table.ts:120,128; connector.ts:90; effects.ts:22; text.ts:157,308,314,321). A string alpha/tint containing a double quote escapes the attribute and injects attacker-chosen OOXML into the deck exported by another user — unsafe input handling / markup injection, in the Security lane. No guard elsewhere sanitizes or coerces these fields.

finding.summary: The new API-side alignment allowlist never runs on header/footer blocks (or on slides text-body blocks), so the same value it rejects can still be persisted through the same endpoint
finding.evidence: `assertValidBlockStyle` is only reached from `assertValidBlock`, and `assertValidDocsBody` (controller.ts:249-251) walks only `body.blocks`. But `writeDocsRoot` also persists `document.header.blocks` and `document.footer.blocks` (`packages/backend/src/yorkie/docs-tree.ts:289-303`, each child built with the same `buildBlockNode`, whose `serializeBlockStyle` writes `alignment: style.alignment` verbatim at `:143`). So `PUT /api/v1/workspaces/:ws/documents/:id/content` with `{"blocks":[],"header":{"marginFromEdge":0,"blocks":[{"id":"b1","type":"paragraph","style":{"alignment":"center\"/><w:jc w:val=\"right"},"inlines":[]}]}}` bypasses the gate entirely, and the value flows to the *same* sink via `DocxExporter.buildHeaderFooterXml` → `blockToXml` → `buildParagraphPropertiesXml`, landing in `word/header1.xml`. The identical hole exists on the slides arm: `assertValidSlidesBody`/`assertValidElement` (controller.ts:415-435) check only `id`/`type`/`frame`, so element text-body blocks carry arbitrary `style.alignment` into `ALGN[...]` in the PPTX exporter. Header/footer blocks also skip every other block check (`id`, `type`, `style`, `inlines`), so a malformed block reaches `buildBlockNode` unguarded. Exploitability of the alignment payload is currently blocked by the exporter-side lookup — but that lookup has the prototype-chain hole reported separately, and the guard reads as covering a sink it does not cover. Fix: run `assertValidBlock` over `body.header?.blocks` / `body.footer?.blocks` (and over slides element text bodies).

verdict.reason:
The finding's premise does not hold in this repository. (1) There is no "new API-side alignment allowlist" in the controller to be bypassed: `assertValidBlock` (packages/backend/src/api/v1/docs-content.controller.ts:254-312) validates shape only, and the comment at :265-270 states explicitly and by design that style *values* are not constrained because "every OOXML sink resolves `alignment` through its own closed lookup". A repo-wide grep for `assertValidBlockStyle` finds it only inside `.agent-review/*` review artifacts, never in source. So the gate the finding says is "bypassed on header/footer" does not exist for body blocks either — there is no asymmetry.

(2) The sink the finding names IS already guarded, and header/footer blocks go through that exact guard. `DocxExporter.buildHeaderFooterXml` (packages/docs/src/export/docx-exporter.ts:360-366) maps each header/footer block through the same `blockToXml`, which resolves alignment via `buildParagraphPropertiesXml` (docx-exporter.ts:186), and that function resolves `style.alignment` through `DOCX_ALIGNMENTS.get(...) ?? 'left'` (packages/docs/src/export/docx-style-map.ts:118-147). The exact payload quoted in the finding (`center"/><w:jc w:val="right`) therefore cannot reach `word/header1.xml`; there is a regression test asserting precisely that (packages/docs/test/export/docx-style-map.test.ts:149-158).

(3) The finding's escape hatch — "that lookup has the prototype-chain hole reported separately" — is false here: both lookups are `Map`s, not object literals. `DOCX_ALIGNMENTS = new Map(...)` (docx-style-map.ts:118) and the slides arm's `ALGN = new Map(...)` consumed as `ALGN.get(block.style.alignment) ?? 'l'` (packages/slides/src/export/pptx/text.ts:69, :99), with the prototype-key cases covered by tests (docx-style-map.test.ts:161-176). `Map.get` returns only own entries, so `toString`/`constructor`/`__proto__` cannot survive the fallback. Slide text-body alignment is closed at its `ALGN[...]` sink for the same reason, so the second arm of the finding also has no vector.

(4) The residual true part — header/footer blocks skip the `id`/`type`/`style`/`inlines` shape checks, so a malformed block can reach `buildBlockNode` (packages/backend/src/yorkie/docs-tree.ts:313-329) — yields a TypeError/HTTP 500 on the caller's own workspace-scoped document (route is behind `CombinedAuthGuard` + `WorkspaceScopeGuard`, controller.ts:67-68), with nothing persisted. That is input-robustness/correctness, not authorization, injection, secrets, or crypto, so it is not blocking under the Security rubric.

mergedFrom.summary: New `isEmptyStoredColor` dereferences a null `StoredColor`, crashing the render path on attacker-controlled slide JSON (stored DoS)

finding.summary: New `isEmptyStoredColor` dereferences an untrusted `StoredColor` without a type guard — a `null` color or an `{ kind: 'srgb', value: <non-string> }` persisted through the content PUT API throws a TypeError inside the paint path, crashing the renderer for every viewer of the document (stored DoS).
finding.evidence: `isEmptyStoredColor` (packages/docs/src/model/color.ts:59-63) does `if (c === undefined) return false;` then `typeof c === 'string' ? ... : c.kind === 'srgb' && c.value.trim() === ''`. For `c === null` (typeof 'object', not undefined) it evaluates `c.kind` → `TypeError: Cannot read properties of null`. For `{ kind: 'srgb', value: 42 }` it evaluates `(42).trim()` → `TypeError: c.value.trim is not a function`. Before this delta the same input was harmless: `resolve(c === '' ? undefined : c)` passed `null` straight to the resolver, and slides' `makeColorResolver` (packages/slides/src/view/canvas/text-renderer.ts:55) returns the theme text color for `c == null`, while `resolveColor` (packages/slides/src/model/theme.ts:102) returns a non-string `value` verbatim without throwing. Attack path: an authenticated caller (workspace member or API key) PUTs a slides body to `PUT /api/v1/workspaces/:ws/documents/:id/content`; `assertValidSlidesBody`/`assertValidElement` (packages/backend/src/api/v1/docs-content.controller.ts:415-435) validate only `id`/`type`/`frame`, and `writeSlidesRoot` assigns `root.slides = document.slides` verbatim (packages/backend/src/yorkie/slides-tree.ts:104), so `slides[i].elements[j].text.blocks[k].inlines[l].style.color = null` (or `{kind:'srgb',value:42}`) is persisted unchanged. Every client that renders the deck reaches `resolveStoredColor` from `paintLayout` (packages/docs/src/view/paint-layout.ts:388, 453, 555), `table-renderer.ts:464/573` and `resolveColorAtPosition` (color.ts:182) and throws, so the canvas render loop dies for all collaborators until the poisoned value is removed out-of-band. Fix: make the guard total (`typeof c !== 'object' || c === null` → false; `typeof c.value === 'string' && c.value.trim() === ''`).

verdict.reason: The quoted vulnerable code does not exist. `isEmptyStoredColor` (packages/docs/src/model/color.ts:67-74) is already total and is literally the fix the finding proposes: line 68 `if (c == null) return true;` catches `null` as well as `undefined` (so `c.kind` is never read on `null`), line 70 rejects non-objects, and line 73 `typeof value !== 'string' || value.trim() === ''` treats `{kind:'srgb', value: 42}` as "no color" without ever calling `(42).trim()`. Both claimed TypeErrors are therefore impossible; each payload resolves to `resolve(undefined)` at color.ts:51, which slides' `makeColorResolver` handles via its `c == null` branch (packages/slides/src/view/canvas/text-renderer.ts:55) returning the theme text color. Grep confirms a single definition of `isEmptyStoredColor` (color.ts:67, used only at color.ts:51), so no other copy carries the described unguarded form, and the string `c === undefined) return false` appears nowhere in the repository. The companion sink `toRgbHexColor` also fails closed on non-strings (color.ts:118). With no dereference of untrusted data at the cited lines, the asserted stored-DoS vector has no enabling line.

finding.summary: PPTX `<a:pPr lvl>` still raw-interpolates untrusted `block.listLevel` in the same function whose color children were just hardened
finding.evidence: `const lvl = block.listLevel ? ` lvl="${block.listLevel}"` : '';` interpolates the model value with no numeric coercion or closed lookup, into `<a:pPr algn="${algn}"${lvl}...>` (line 114). Unlike docs blocks (whose Yorkie Tree attributes are re-read with `Number(attrs.listLevel)` — frontend yorkie-doc-store.ts:459, backend docs-tree.ts:414), slides text bodies are plain JSON persisted verbatim by `writeSlidesRoot` (packages/backend/src/yorkie/slides-tree.ts:104) with no per-block validation in `assertValidElement` (docs-content.controller.ts:415-435). Vector: PUT slides content with `data.blocks[0].listLevel = '0"><a:buNone/><a:pPr algn="l'`; a victim exporting the deck gets attacker-chosen OOXML written into `ppt/slides/slideN.xml`. Same defect class as the `<w:jc>` case this change fixed; `<a:alpha val="${c.alpha}"/>` and the lumMod/tint/shade siblings in packages/slides/src/export/pptx/color.ts:25-29 interpolate model values raw for the same reason.

verdict.reason: The finding's central claim is factually false in this tree. The quoted line `const lvl = block.listLevel ? ` lvl="${block.listLevel}"` : '';` does not exist in packages/slides/src/export/pptx/text.ts. Instead, text.ts:82-86 defines `listLevelAttr()`, which does `Math.trunc(Number(listLevel))`, drops the attribute on non-finite/<=0, and clamps with `Math.min(8, n)` before interpolating; text.ts:100 is the sole caller feeding the `<a:pPr ... lvl>` sink at text.ts:134. The claimed payload `'0"><a:buNone/><a:pPr algn="l'` coerces to NaN and the attribute is omitted, so no OOXML can be injected via block.listLevel. The doc comment at text.ts:76-81 explicitly names the untrusted-content-PUT threat model, i.e. this exact hardening is already applied — the finding appears to describe a pre-fix state. The sibling `algn` value is also closed-set (ALGN Map, text.ts:69-74, 99), and other attributes in the same function are numerically coerced (Math.round/ptToHundredths) or escaped via escapeXmlAttr (text.ts:168, 325, 335). The finding's trailing aside about color.ts:25-29 does exist as raw interpolation, but those fields are typed `number` in both ThemeColor (model/theme.ts:54-60) and StoredColor (docs/src/model/color.ts:7-10) and are produced by numeric import parsing (import/pptx/color.ts:170-179, attrInt/100000); it is a different file and sink and does not support the asserted text.ts `lvl` vector.
